competitors.title: Building a human-in-the-loop approval queue for an AI agent
key_points: Fault line = small set of actions that produce real damage if wrong: financial transactions, customer-visible mutations, irreversible deletes, outbound API calls without undo

approval_queue table with Drizzle ORM schema: id, action_type, payload, before_state (jsonb snapshot), after_state (jsonb snapshot), requested_by, requested_at, reason, status, decided_by, decided_at, decision_note, executed_at, execution_error
Agent dispatch loop checks GATED_ACTIONS set; gated actions enqueue instead of executing, ungated actions execute with audit trail
Review UI: one-tap approve/reject with structured diff visible without scrolling; rejects require a note that feeds back into agent's context
Execute on approve (not cron-based) to avoid race conditions from lag between approve-click and execution
Demotion ladder: action classes graduate from queue to audit-after-the-fact based on track record of approvals with no rejections

competitors.title: AI Agent Approval Queue: How to Review High-Risk Actions Without Killing Throughput
key_points: Queue as holding layer between agent recommendation and real-world action when crossing a risk boundary
Three classes of queue work: policy-bound actions, high-risk exceptions, human-value edge cases
Each queue item must show: proposed action, reason for review, source evidence, risk summary, available actions
Most queues fail from: too much landing in queue, no useful context for reviewers, no priority model, no timeout policy
Tighten autonomy boundary upstream — push routine work to auto-approval, conditional approval, or hard blocks
Separate approvals from failures: use different lanes for approval-required, data-missing, tool-failed, state-conflict, manual-investigation
Every item needs priority level + SLA/deadline; track items/day, approval rate, median review time, stale items, escalation reasons

competitors.title: Tool Approval and Human-in-the-Loop in Microsoft Agent Framework
key_points: MAF IChatClient middleware pipeline supports DelegatingChatClient pattern for tool approval interception
ToolApprovalMiddleware inspects FunctionCallContent before execution, sets Exception on rejected calls
Selective approval via AIFunction metadata (REQUIRES_APPROVAL=true in description text)
Rejection is not a dead end — feed rejection reason back into session so agent proposes alternative path
Applicable to: financial transactions, file system modifications, email/messaging, external API writes, batch operations

competitors.title: Build the approval queue before you build the agent
key_points: Proposed action as structured object: workflow, sourceRecord, proposedAction (type/to/subject/body), riskLevel, requiresApproval, modelRationale
Risk levels: low (summarize, draft notes, classify), medium (draft customer comms, update CRM), high (send money, change access, delete, publish)
Model can suggest risk but application overrides based on action type, destination, or dollar threshold
OWASP prompt injection mitigation: approval queue gives second place to apply rules outside the prompt
Approval screen answers: what is AI trying to do? why? what source material? what could go wrong? what happens after approve?
Audit trail as event log: draft_created, edited, approved, executed — making failures diagnosable
Autonomy granted by evidence, not enthusiasm: measure which action types approved without edits, then grant automation

competitors.title: LangGraph Interrupts — Human-in-the-Loop Patterns
key_points: Dynamic interrupts via interrupt() function — pause at any point in graph execution, not just before/after nodes
Checkpointing saves exact graph state with thread_id as persistent cursor for resume
Approval workflow: interrupt() with payload on stream.interrupts, resume with Command(resume=True/False)
Multiple parallel interrupts can be resumed simultaneously by mapping interrupt IDs to resume values
Review and edit pattern: let humans modify LLM outputs before continuing execution
Event streaming loop: consume messages token-by-token, detect interrupts via stream.interrupted, resume with Command(resume=...)

competitors.title: OpenAI Agents SDK — Guardrails and Human Review
key_points: OpenAI provides guardrails framework and human review capabilities in their Agents SDK
Guardrails validate agent inputs and outputs, with approval gates for tool calls
Function calling 5-step flow: define tools, model requests tool call, execute code, send output back, receive final response
Parallel tool calls and structured outputs supported in the review pipeline
